content.text: One project. Every element. A coherent experience.

Experience Lab is a private working case study for evaluating the Ramzy Studio editor as a complete product. It brings writing, imagery, media, structured layouts and supporting documents into one coherent narrative.
The quality of the experience lives in the transitions between elements.
Product design · Design systems · UX research
Consistent appearance, discoverable controls, reliable saving
Can an author move between elements without relearning the interface?
Do mixed layouts remain readable and editable on touch devices?
Does saved content match the preview?
All examples are synthetic review fixtures. No outcome is a measured product result.
Individually useful components can feel inconsistent when their typography, spacing, controls and empty states are combined. This project makes those differences visible in context.
Familiar structure: consistent spacing and hierarchy.
Predictable actions: controls follow the selected content.
Honest feedback: loading, saving and errors remain clear.
Use this section to check long lines, selection, cursor movement and transitions between text and media.

A deliberately longer paragraph tests wrapping in narrow columns. Check that the line height feels consistent with neighbouring blocks and that tapping between words places the cursor where expected. This text is editable and contains no hidden behaviour.
Start on desktop, repeat on iPad and phone, then compare Build and Preview. Open each toolbar, edit one value and reload after saving.
Record the actual result in the checklist.
The same artwork appears as a single image, grid and album so differences in framing, captions and controls are easy to compare.

Context: this is a shared review workspace.
Note: use the same spacing rules across every element.
Success state specimen — no test result is implied.
Warning state specimen — check contrast and icon alignment.
Error state specimen — check that the next action is clear.
Each row increases the layout density. Check reading order, toolbar placement, drag handles and responsive stacking.
A readable summary next to supporting media.
The wider column carries the story. The sidebar provides concise context without competing with it.

flowchart TD
  A[Compose content] --> B[Save draft]
  B --> C[Open preview]
  C --> D{Review passed?}
  D -->|Yes| E[Record result]
  D -->|No| A
where p is passed checks and t is total checks. No score has been measured.

content.text: The brief and checklist are local project attachments. Provider-specific blocks below are intentionally empty authoring states: add your own shareable source to test that provider without substituting an unrelated demo.
Mark a check complete only after observing the result on the device.
Open every element toolbar and use one control.
Edit text and media metadata, save and reload.
Reorder an image and a playlist item.
Test media playback, seeking and captions.
Check adjacent grids and dense columns on touch.
Open the PDF, download a file and edit both diagrams.
Add provider URLs and test their embedded content.
Expected behaviour: describe the intended experience.
Reproduction: record the element, device, browser and steps.
Review the complete project before changing individual components. Prioritise problems that repeat across element families, then retest the same journey.

This fixture includes every insertion family exposed by the portfolio menu. Seven external provider blocks cover empty/source-entry states until valid URLs are supplied. Workspace-only relations such as Bases, subpages and mentions are outside the portable portfolio contract.
All device checks remain pending until performed. The importer verifies document storage, not visual behaviour.
This is a synthetic quality-review fixture. Passing tests must be recorded from actual observations, not inferred from the sample content.
